business: Telo Pilates Club — reformer pilates studio, Vektra district, Podgorica (Montenegro). Outreach concept page; the studio's real public assets are an Instagram profile and an Alteg.io booking tenant.
artDirection: A near-black "ink" poster ground dominates, with the studio's butter yellow used only as accent — type, a radius-0 CTA slab, or a stroke — and a chalk off-white as the neutral beat between ink bands. One typeface only, Albert Sans, at extreme weight contrast (900 for every display line, regular for reading), all-lowercase with a terminal full stop echoing the studio's wordmark. No photography at all; the sole picture is a line-drawn "reformer carriage travelling its rail" mark that draws itself on scroll and repeats twice.
strengths: Ink-dominant poster palette sampled from the studio's own wordmark tile — butter appears only on ink, never as a fill on light. A real, committed colour decision rather than a default dark mode. KEEP.

Single-family type system (Albert Sans 900/400, no second 'editorial' serif, no mono family). A geometric grotesque at poster weight is the right voice for a movement studio, and refusing a second family is the discipline the previously rejected pass lacked. KEEP the one-family rule.

The data layer's ethic: no mirrored timetable, no invented prices, no fake testimonials, no named instructors, Polestar claim rendered with its attribution intact ('Studio navodi da...'). Honest and it reads as trustworthy. KEEP.

The formats section answers a real job-to-be-done — 'which of these five names do I click in the booking calendar' — and each line describes who else is in the room rather than marketing the class. 'izaberi format, pa termin.' is the strongest copy on the page. KEEP the concept.

CTA discipline: one label ('Rezerviši čas'), one destination, one visual treatment (butter slab, radius 0, uppercase tracked) across header, hero, sticky bar and close. The primary action is never ambiguous. KEEP.

Engineering restraint: scroll-driven CSS animation with zero JS, settled state as the reduced-motion and no-support default; two focus-ring variants tuned to ink vs chalk grounds; sticky bar correctly gated with tabIndex/aria-hidden and suppressed over the closing CTA and footer. KEEP all of it.
The component-level slop list is genuinely respected: no rounded cards, no shadows, no glow, no badges, no stat blocks, no testimonial grid, no emoji, no gradient. KEEP.

issues.issue: The page's one subject-grounded signature element does not read as anything. On desktop (hero, y≈330 in the 1440 shot) it renders as a faint asymmetric hairline squiggle — a 1.25px rail with a 4.5px arc stretched across ~360px — indistinguishable from a stray rule or a chart glitch. On phone the frame collapses to 240x36px: the 12px round 'carriage' dot and the ~11px end tick land at the same coordinate and merge into a single lollipop/bone blob, so the 'two fixed stops + a carriage between them' reading is destroyed. The two instances also disagree with each other — the hero mark is a hairline, the closing echo (trackEcho stroke-width 10) is a fat confident arc — so the signature is not even self-consistent. The 200-word comment block above RangeMark describes an idea far more ambitious than what any viewport actually shows. This is the single element carrying the entire visual load of a photograph-free page.
issues.where: RangeMark component, page.tsx:66-101; .trackTick/.trackStroke/.trackEnd stroke weights, telo.module.css:50-98; hero instance page.tsx:151, close instance page.tsx:305-307

issues.issue: The page is information-poor to the point where it does not beat the studio's existing Instagram bio link. There is no price, no duration, no capacity, no class times, no opening hours, no street address, no phone, no photograph of the room, the reformers, or a single body in motion. Every concrete question a first-timer has is deferred to a third-party booking system that opens in a new tab. data.ts documents a principled reason for each omission, and those reasons are individually defensible — but the cumulative result is a page whose sales argument to the client ('your site should be more useful than your link-in-bio') is not actually demonstrated. A pilates studio sells the room and the machine; this page shows neither and substitutes abstract nouns.
issues.where: Whole page; data.ts:35-98 (formats carry only a 'setting' line) and data.ts:112-135 researchOnly

issues.issue: The formats board has a ~470px dead gutter on desktop. md:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_17rem] gives the 1fr column far more width than the longest format name needs, so 'grupni reformer' sits at the far left and its description floats at the far right with half a screen of nothing between them; the eye has to jump the gap five times. Worse, all five rows are visually identical — same 2px rules, same 900 weight, same scale, same rhythm — so there is no signal that 'grupni reformer' is the entry format most visitors will book and 'healthy spine' is a niche one. This is a uniform card grid rotated ninety degrees: the hairline-rule list grammar the house standard explicitly bans, with no per-row differentiation to earn it.
issues.where: Formats section, page.tsx:194-207 (ul/li grid), rendered at desktop y≈950-1700

issues.issue: The board's headline promises 'izaberi format, pa termin' (choose a format, then a time) but choosing does nothing. No row is a link, no row carries a per-format action into the booking system, and there is no anchor from a format to the CTA. The one interactive promise the page makes is a dead end — the visitor reads five names, then has to scroll past three more sections to find a generic booking button and re-find the format by name inside an unfamiliar calendar, which is the exact problem the section exists to solve.

Two chalk sections stack back-to-back with no divider, producing roughly 160-180px of empty off-white between the last 'prvi čas' sentence and the 'GDJE' kicker. It does not read as breathing room — it reads as a hole, and it makes 'gdje' look like an orphaned continuation of the first-visit section rather than its own beat. The 'prvi čas' grid compounds it: column one holds a single short line, so the whole three-column block is ragged along its bottom edge with a void beneath it.
issues.where: page.tsx:244 (first-visit section, py-20) abutting page.tsx:267 (location section, py-20); desktop shot y≈2280-2450

issues.issue: The 1/2/3 ghost numerals are the banned decorative-numbering idiom, and they fail on their own terms too. Set at ink/15 (~1.15:1 against chalk) they render as pale printing artifacts, not as a designed element — on phone they are barely perceptible next to their sentences. They also carry no information: the three items are not a sequence ('wear comfortable clothes', 'arrive a few minutes early', 'the instructor walks you through the machine' have no order), so the numbering asserts a progression that does not exist. Removing them costs the page nothing.

Hierarchy is inverted in the ink method band, and it is the shortest band on the page (~300px vs the hero's ~700px). The three genuinely differentiating facts live here — Polestar methodology, the five-piece apparatus inventory, trilingual instruction — and the least important of them gets the loudest treatment: 'mne / eng / rus' is set at clamp(2.5rem,10vw,5rem) black, while the Polestar claim sits at 1.3rem and the apparatus list (reformer, tower, chair, spine corrector, strunjača — the most concrete, most physical, most studio-specific content on the entire page) is set as 0.95rem tracked caps in muted-ink, the visual weight of a legal footnote. Additionally the two halves of the top row are different colours (butter left, muted-ink right) on one baseline, so the right half reads as disabled.

'mne / eng / rus' at poster scale in the accent colour reads unmistakably as a language switcher — three locale codes separated by slashes is the universal UI signature for exactly that. It is a non-interactive

. On both phone and desktop the first instinct is to click it. A false affordance on the only high-contrast element in that band.

At 390px the equipment string breaks mid-item: 'REFORMER · TOWER · CHAIR · SPINE / CORRECTOR · STRUNJAČA'. Because the separator is a mid-dot and the wrap falls inside 'SPINE CORRECTOR', the phone reader sees six apparatus items instead of five, one of them called 'SPINE' and another 'CORRECTOR'. The inventory is factually misread at the most common viewport.
issues.where: method.equipment.join(' · '), page.tsx:225; data.ts:83; phone shot y≈1790

issues.issue: The studio's brand colour is entirely absent from roughly 55% of the page. Chalk (#f7f7f2) is a plain off-white and butter (#fafbd4) is used only on ink, so the formats board, the first-visit section, the location band and the footer — the whole light half — carry zero studio identity and could belong to any business. The palette has three tokens but the light sections effectively use one, which is why the chalk stretches feel like a different, blander site pasted between the ink posters.
issues.where: telo.module.css:23-36 token definitions; all bg-[var(--telo-chalk)] sections, page.tsx:182, 244, 267, 331

issues.issue: The page runs on two alternating templates and nothing else: ink poster (big lowercase headline left, mark, paragraph + CTA right) and chalk left-aligned list. The closing section is a structural rerun of the hero — same grid ratio, same headline scale, same mark, same right-column paragraph-then-butter-CTA. Every single section uses the identical max-w-6xl container, identical px-5/sm:px-8, identical left rail; there is not one full-bleed moment, one crop, one overlap, one asymmetry beyond a 2-column split, or one change of measure. Scroll density is therefore monotonous even though the ink/chalk alternation is trying to create rhythm.
issues.where: Every <section> container, page.tsx:139, 183, 218, 245, 268, 299; hero (138-177) vs close (298-328)

issues.issue: The lowercase + terminal-full-stop + font-black treatment is applied to all six display lines ('kontrola. snaga. pokret.', 'izaberi format, pa termin.', 'kako izgleda prvi čas.', 'vektra, podgorica.', 'telo u pokretu.', 'telo pilates club.'). What starts as a wordmark echo becomes a tic by the third repetition. More damagingly, font-black is used for the wordmark, every h1/h2/h3, the language codes, the ghost numerals and the footer mark — so weight can no longer signal importance anywhere on the page, and hierarchy collapses onto font-size alone. That is the mechanical cause of the method-band inversion above.

The hero's largest type says the least. 'kontrola. snaga. pokret.' at clamp(3.25rem,15vw,9rem) is three abstract nouns that would fit a gym, a physio clinic, a martial arts dojo or a running club unchanged — nothing in it is reformer pilates, nothing is Telo, nothing is Podgorica. The specific, ownable facts (Polestar method, five formats, trilingual, reformer/tower/chair/spine corrector) are all buried below the fold at body scale. The first screen therefore spends its entire visual budget on generic mood.

The location section is a hierarchy inversion and an unanswered question. 'vektra, podgorica.' gets clamp(2.25rem,7vw,4rem) poster type to state a neighbourhood name — no street, no map, no directions, no hours, no phone — while the only actionable thing in the band (the Instagram link, which is genuinely the studio's real contact channel) is set small and pushed to the far right edge. Semantics are inverted too: the

is the 0.72rem 'GDJE' kicker while the visible headline is a

, so the document outline and the visual outline disagree.

issues.issue: The phone primary CTA is timid at the exact moment of decision. 'Rezerviši čas' is an inline-flex px-9 button roughly 200px wide sitting under a 15vw headline in a 390px column, so the page's single most important action is visually smaller than any headline word above it. issues.issue: At 390px the hero eyebrow 'REFORMER PILATES · VEKTRA, PODGORICA' wraps with 'PODGORICA' orphaned alone on line two. At 0.72rem with 0.28em tracking this two-line caps block is the first content under the wordmark and it reads as clutter rather than orientation.

The rail in the RangeMark overhangs both end stops by ~42px at desktop (path starts at x=0 but the first tick is at x=140, last tick at x=1060 with the rail running to x=1200). The stubs sticking out past both stops read as an unresolved drawing rather than a deliberate 'the rail continues' gesture, because nothing else on the page uses overhang as a motif.

The closing band leaves roughly 230px of empty ink above the right-hand column. lg:items-end bottom-aligns the paragraph+CTA stack against the headline+mark stack, so the right column floats low in a large void with nothing occupying its upper two thirds.

The formats intro paragraph is constrained to max-w-md inside a max-w-2xl block under a much wider headline, so on desktop it wraps into three short lines and leaves a ragged L-shaped void to its right. The measure fights the headline it sits under instead of relating to it.

At 390px the header is a near-empty ~60px band: the CTA is hidden below the sm breakpoint, so the wordmark sits alone on the left with the entire right half blank. The page's most valuable persistent real estate does nothing until the sticky bar appears much further down.

--telo-muted (#6b6c5c, ~5.1:1 on chalk) carries all light-section body copy — the format descriptions, the intro paragraph, the location line, the footer disclaimer. It passes AA but it is conspicuously the weakest contrast on a page that otherwise trades in 17:1 maximum contrast, so the light sections read greyer and softer than the art direction intends.

Two mono-caps kickers survive from the editorial grammar the house standard rejects: the hero eyebrow and the 'GDJE' label, both at 0.72rem/0.28em tracking. Two instances is restrained, but 'GDJE' in particular is pure decoration — it labels a section whose content already says it is a place.
issues.where: const eyebrow, page.tsx:29; used at 141 and 271

issues.issue: preserveAspectRatio='none' squashes the arc's strokeLinecap='round' terminals into ovals and distorts the curve's tangents non-uniformly, which is part of why the mark reads as a wobble rather than a controlled travel path. Visible on close inspection at every viewport.

In the footer, 'Koncept: VibeLab' is bottom-aligned to the right on sm+ but the left block is three lines tall, so the credit hangs in isolation far from anything it relates to, with a wide empty span between.

verdict: This is art-directed, not generated-by-default — the ink-dominant poster ground with butter as accent-only, the single-family black-weight typography, and the refusal to invent a timetable are all real decisions with a point of view, and the component-level slop list is genuinely clean. But it lands on a different fashionable template rather than on this business: strip the words and the page reads equally well as a coffee roaster, a barbershop or a techno label, because nothing in it is specifically reformer pilates. The one element that was supposed to fix that — the carriage-on-a-rail mark — fails to render legibly at any viewport, collapsing to a hairline on desktop and a blob on phone, so the page is left carrying its entire visual load on typography alone while also having no photograph, no price, no hours and no timetable. Hierarchy then works against it: font-black is the default weight everywhere, so size is the only remaining signal, which is why three locale codes shout at 5rem while the Polestar claim and the apparatus inventory whisper. A top-tier small-business site would answer what a first-timer actually asks and would make the formats board actionable; right now the page states five format names, promises 'choose a format, then a time', and then hands the visitor a generic off-site link four times.
